correctness.rationale: The three commutation equations are derived from 4x4 unipotent multiplication. Conjugating Y varies its middle entries linearly in three first-superdiagonal parameters; the induced scalar correction is either surjective or zero. The seven disjoint primary cases exactly cover all coefficients, including characteristic two. Summation gives the stated rho polynomial, while independent K=0 counting yields cp and a positive factored gap. Exhaustive q=2,3,4 checks and independent literal group 4x4 multiplication q=2,3 agree. The paper discrepancy in an ordinary cp table is disclosed, and the literal enumeration independently confirms the companion formula at q=3.

evidence: Kaur–Sharma–Singh arXiv:2006.01493 provides branching matrices and probabilities for literally commuting tuples in UT_4(q), odd q. Section 8 gives ordinary cp2 rather than conjugate-commuting rho. The 2011 finite-group probability paper provides general bounds and symmetric-group asymptotics.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The ordinary commuting probability and simultaneous commuting-tuple class enumeration do not measure the Boolean existence of a commuting pair of representatives for two independently fixed conjugacy classes. Their statements neither dominate nor coincide with the new rho formula. A general unlocated character-theoretic theorem remains a residual risk.

originality.rationale: The original 2007 commuting-conjugates relation, 2011 rho paper, and 2020 UT4 branching computations address distinct statements; inspected the closest primary full texts, compared logical implications and equivalent formulations, and searched exact/alias queries in accessible mathematical records. Did not identify the exact rho(UT4(Fq)) formula. Source discrepancies and inaccessible plausible material leave provisional historical priority.
residual_risks: Historical literature may contain a broader unlocated enumeration of commuting conjugacy-class pairs that implies this special case.

A 2020 ordinary commuting-probability table for UT4(q) disagrees with literal multiplication for q=3 (53 vs 57 classes). The discrepancy is independently quantified but not bibliographically resolved. It does not assert or determine the rho statistic.

value.rationale: Conjugacy-relaxed commutation is a natural group probability developed in the 2011 literature. UT_4 is the first genuinely class-three upper unitriangular family, unlike the class-two UT_3 where rho=cp. A closed polynomial for every prime-power field and a strictly positive gap asymptotically of order 1/q versus cp of order 1/q^3 quantify a structural transition; no arbitrary slice or known-table recomputation is needed.
